sentences.text: Lucasuchus is an extinct genus belonging to the group of armored reptiles known as aetosaurs.

This animal possessed elongated horns on its lateral osteoderms, a feature shared with other members of the subfamily Desmatosuchinae, while its paramedian osteoderms featured large conical projections unlike the low pyramidal bosses of Longosuchus, and it lacked notches on the spikes of its lateral osteoderms.
It belongs to the subfamily Desmatosuchinae, and the type species of the genus Lucasuchus is Lucasuchus hunti.

The genus Lucasuchus was named in 1995 in honor of the American paleontologist Spencer G. Lucas, after fossils were discovered in the Bull Canyon Formation of the Dockum Group in Quay County, New Mexico.

All known specimens of Lucasuchus date to the Norian stage of the Late Triassic, though the time range for Lucasuchus is estimated to be between 237 and 227.3 million years ago during the Carnian age.

Researchers have debated whether Lucasuchus represents a sexual dimorph of Longosuchus meadei or an ontogenetic stage of that species, despite the fact that several characteristics suggest that Lucasuchus is a distinct species rather than a morphological variation of Longosuchus meadei.
